chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdul-Sammad ibn Bashir, from Atiyya, the brother of Abu Al-Maghra', who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'The companions of Al-Mughira are forbidding the eating of the Qadeed (dried meat) which fire has not touched.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with eating it.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابَ الْمُغِيرَةِ: The companions of Al-Mughira, a group known for specific religious opinions.
key_terms.الْقَدِيدِ: Dried meat or preserved meat, typically prepared by salting and drying.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible, a common legal ruling phrase.
key_terms.لَمْ تَمَسَّهُ النَّارُ: Which fire has not touched, referring to the lack of cooking or fire-drying.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat dried meat that has not been touched by fire according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the consumption of 'Qadeed' (sun-dried or air-dried meat) without fire, demonstrating the principle of *al-asl fi al-akl al-ibahah* (the default permissibility of food) against the restrictive opinions of the *Ashab al-Mughira*. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding food preservation methods, distinguishing between mere drying and the necessity of cooking for permissibility.
